What Is Breast Augmentation?

Breast augmentation (augmentation mammoplasty) enhances breast size, shape, and projection using FDA-approved silicone gel implants, cohesive "gummy bear" implants, saline implants, or fat transfer (autologous fat grafting). The right choice depends on your starting anatomy, goals, lifestyle, and tissue thickness.

At our Kondapur clinic, Dr. Ram Prabhu personalises every augmentation — the implant size, shape (round vs anatomical), placement (sub-glandular vs sub-muscular), and incision location are all selected based on your body proportions and aesthetic preferences. We use 3D imaging during consultation so you can preview results before deciding.

Modern breast augmentation is not about going as large as possible — it is about achieving balanced, natural proportions that suit your frame. Most Indian women choose moderate augmentation in the 250-350cc range that delivers a feminine, fitted-clothing look without obvious "enhanced" appearance.

Augmentation can also be combined with a breast lift (mastopexy) when there is sagging, or with breast reconstruction after mastectomy.

Causes & Indications

Common Causes

  • Naturally small breast size (micromastia)
  • Asymmetry between left and right breasts
  • Volume loss after pregnancy and breastfeeding
  • Volume loss after significant weight loss
  • Reconstructive needs after mastectomy
  • Tubular breast deformity
  • Concerns about clothing fit and proportions
  • Confidence and self-image concerns

Signs You May Need Breast Augmentation

  • Difficulty finding well-fitting bras and tops
  • Self-consciousness in swimwear or fitted clothing
  • Asymmetry that requires padding on one side
  • Loss of upper-pole fullness after pregnancy
  • Feeling of disproportion between breasts and hips
  • Tubular or constricted breast shape since puberty

What Happens on the Day of Breast Augmentation

  1. Step 1 — Sizer Selection (in consultation)

    Sizers are tried during consultation. 3D simulation shows expected appearance. Implant choice finalised.

  2. Step 2 — Arrival & Markings (45 min)

    Pre-op photographs. Detailed markings while sitting and standing — incision location, implant pocket boundaries.

  3. Step 3 — Anaesthesia (15 min)

    General anaesthesia administered by a board-certified anaesthetist.

  4. Step 4 — Incision & Pocket (60 min)

    Incision via inframammary fold (under breast), peri-areolar (around nipple), or trans-axillary (armpit). Implant pocket created — sub-glandular or sub-muscular.

  5. Step 5 — Implant Insertion (15-30 min)

    Implants inserted using a sterile no-touch technique (Keller funnel). Position verified for symmetry.

  6. Step 6 — Closure (30 min)

    Tissue closed in layers with absorbable sutures. Surgical bra applied.

  7. Step 7 — Recovery (3-4 hrs)

    Observation in recovery. Most patients walk out same day or after one night observation.

Recovery Timeline

Day 0

Surgery day

Mild-moderate soreness. Sleep elevated and on back. Surgical bra 24/7.

Day 1-3

Initial recovery

Soreness peaks Day 2-3. Pain medication for 5-7 days. Light walking encouraged.

Day 5-7

Return to work

Most desk-job patients return to work. No heavy lifting. Driving cleared.

Week 2-3

Light exercise

Walking and gentle cardio okay. No upper body or chest exercises yet.

Week 4-6

Most activities resumed

Cardio fully cleared. Light upper body permitted. Implants begin to settle into final position.

Month 3

"Drop and fluff"

Implants settle into natural position. Final shape becoming evident.

Month 6

Final result

Implants fully settled. Final breast shape visible. Long-term result.
